title: Iterative quantum algorithms for the minimum vertex cover problem based on continuous-time quantum walks
authors: Ruben Pariente Bassa, Finley A. Quinton, Franz G. Fuchs, Pascal Halffmann
abstract: We introduce a constraint-preserving hybrid quantum-classical greedy framework for the minimum vertex cover problem, which extends directly to maximum independent set by bitwise complementation. The framework uses projected Pauli-X terms whose sum preserves the feasible subspace and acts within it exactly as the adjacency matrix of a layered graph of feasible covers. This graph is connected, so every feasible cover is linked to the configuration containing all vertices by a sequence of allowed single-vertex flips. Starting from this configuration, the corresponding continuous-time quantum walk propagates amplitude into layers containing progressively smaller covers. We rank vertices using either their marginal cover probabilities or the expected cover size obtained after fixing each candidate vertex in the cover, and use these rankings to guide recursive greedy reductions. Across several random-graph families, with walk times fixed using independent calibration ensembles, the quantum-informed algorithms achieve lower mean approximation ratios and solve a larger fraction of instances optimally than their corresponding classical greedy baselines. The conditioned-energy strategy performs best on the tested instances and retains algorithmic performance close to the exact continuous-time limit under low-depth Trotterisation. For bounded-degree graphs, each Trotter layer has circuit depth independent of system size, and the framework requires neither penalty terms nor variational training.
summary: This paper introduces a novel hybrid quantum-classical framework to solve the Minimum Vertex Cover problem using continuous-time quantum walks. The CTQW evolves within the subspace of feasible vertex covers, generating quantum metrics that guide a greedy reduction process. The results show these quantum-informed methods outperform classical heuristics on random graph ensembles.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-complete Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC) problem by developing a quantum algorithm framework.
main_result: Quantum-informed greedy algorithms utilizing continuous-time quantum walks achieve lower mean approximation ratios and solve more instances optimally than classical greedy baselines on random graphs.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical approach uses CTQWs evolving within the feasible subspace of MVC, guiding a recursive greedy reduction based on quantum state observables.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) operating on a graph derived from the feasible state space of vertex covers. The dynamics are constrained using projected Pauli operators to maintain feasibility within the Hilbert space.
key_observables: Marginal cover probabilities ($P_i$) and expected cover sizes ($E_i$), used as quantum-derived scores for greedy selection.
important_parameters: Walk time ($t$), Trotterization step size ($p$), graph structure (e.g., bounded degree, random families).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the induced feasible-state graph is connected and that local observables derived from the CTQW can effectively guide a greedy search.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the iterative process linking the input graph to the state space graph via CTQW, and show entropy scaling related to quantum walk dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for constraining CTQWs to the feasible subspace. It then details the hybrid greedy algorithm using quantum observables (QPG/QEG) and analyzes its performance against classical methods on various graph families.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, resource-aware application of constrained quantum dynamics (CTQW) for combinatorial optimization, which is highly relevant to developing practical quantum algorithms beyond simple Hamiltonian simulation.
